course_title: Special Topics in Biology: Intro to Bioinformatics
subject: BIOL
course_description: A course on topics of special biological interest, designed for Biology majors elective credit. This course is repeatable when the topic varies.
course_notes: (Same as CS 485 and CS 584 (not cross listed). For the graduate version (CS 584), a weekly one-hour journal club is added. Prerequisites (equivalent or higher): Biol 141/142; Chem 150, Math 116, and DS 100. This course introduces biologists and computer scientists to the computational approaches that make modern biological data usable. We begin with sequence analysis: gene finding and alignment algorithms. We then turn to sequence signatures, domains/motifs, and phylogenomics. The course also covers structural bioinformatics and deep learning approaches to structure prediction, metagenomics, gene expression, single cell analysis, and genomic variation, concluding with disease gene prioritization and precision medicine. Throughout, we consider how machine learning methods are applied to biological questions and how their results should be evaluated. The emphasis is on what algorithms are and why methods work rather than how to run them. Weekly hands-on sessions aim to develop Python skills and familiarize students with existing bioinformatics infrastructure.
